climb.rationale: Index of coincidence first, then the published n-gram counts, which is the ordering Ostwald and Weierud describe. Measured at 167 letters with ten pairs: n-grams alone from the identity plugboard recover the exact plugboard on 3 of 8 key draws; seeding with an index-of-coincidence climb recovers 8 of 8 for 1.6x the work.

positive_controls.rationale: The five independently solved 1941 Army plaintexts Phase 7 already uses, each kept as its own message with its own indicator and enciphered by enigma.EnigmaI under one shared ten-pair daily key. That is the real Army situation: several short messages under one key. An earlier version of this control concatenated the five into two messages at the target lengths and failed, because the junctions between unrelated messages are n-grams no Army text contains; the concatenated form was not a legitimate control and was replaced rather than reinterpreted.

key.plugboard: AV BS CG DL FU HZ IN KM OW RX

positive_controls.rationale: Three messages at exactly the target lengths 167, 107 and 97, from constructed Army-style text that cannot overlap the published n-gram counts. Trades authenticity for a guarantee of no training overlap, so the two controls fail in different ways if either weakness matters.

key.plugboard: AN BY CF DR GJ HS IL KM PV QZ

hypothesis: The two crib-free steps still open for BYQMZ cover different keys, and a planted-key control can say which pays more per host-hour. Among 167-letter draws that neither the whole-message nor the W = 117 middle-past-notch climb detects (the planted-key stand-in for 'phase1-body-direct-sweep-v2 and v3 both null'): (i) the middle-complete ring rule with the W = 117 climb detects at least half of the unperturbed ones; (ii) for one-indel draws whose indel falls in the middle third (letters 56 to 111), the same arm detects at most 20%, while an oracle that undoes the indel at its true position, sweeping the middle-past-notch rule with the whole-message climb, detects at least 60%.
refuted_by: Any of: C1 below 50%, C2 above 20%, C3 below 60% (the three conditional predictions in conditional_analysis, scored by scripts/conditional_power.py on strata of at least 25 draws; a smaller stratum is 'not estimable' and refutes nothing). A refutation of C1 drops the middle-complete rule as a candidate; a refutation of C3 drops a split-point climb. The marginal predictions in end_to_end_power.predictions each refute only themselves.

end_to_end_power.rationale: phase1-end-to-end-power-v1 measured a middle_complete arm (whole-message climb, planted right position only, 40 draws): 39 of 40 clean, 11 of 40 with one indel, against 33 of 40 and 6 of 40 for middle_past_notch on the same draws. That is a rate against the planted key's neighbourhood and says nothing about the keys the two completed sweeps (v2 whole message, v3 W = 117) already covered, which is what decides whether nine times the settings is worth it. The slice then lacked the neighbouring right positions, which raised the past-notch indel rate from 15% to 41% when added (phase1-windowed-climb-power-v1), so its indel figure for the complete rule is probably low as well. This control runs the complete rule with the W = 117 climb and the neighbouring right positions, on the same draws as the two past-notch arms, so that every comparison is paired and the draws the past-notch arms miss can be isolated. A split-point climb (the head at the swept setting, the tail at the setting one keystroke away, a searched split) does not exist. The oracle arm bounds it from above: it is handed the true indel position and kind, sweeps the past-notch slice with the whole-message climb, and so shows how many of the keys the completed sweeps miss are recoverable at all once the indel stops mattering. A real search for the position would do no better and pays for the search in its null.

predictions.statement: The whole-message past-notch climb detects at least 80% of unperturbed draws (88.8% in phase1-windowed-climb-power-v1).
The W = 117 past-notch climb detects at least 45% of single-indel draws (56.3% there).
The whole-message complete rule detects at least 90% of unperturbed draws (39 of 40 in phase1-end-to-end-power-v1, interval 87.1 to 99.6).
The complete rule with the W = 117 climb detects at least 85% of unperturbed draws.
With the indel undone at its true position, the whole-message past-notch sweep detects at least 60% of single-indel draws.
On single-indel draws the oracle arm detects at least 15 points more than the W = 117 past-notch climb.

end_to_end_power.right_neighbours_rationale: The tail window decrypts cleanly only at the setting one keystroke away from the planted one (the right position one further for a deletion, one back for an insertion). A complete sweep enumerates every right position, so it always visits that setting; the slice includes the planted right position and both neighbours for every arm, so the whole-message arm is measured on the same slice as the windowed ones. v1 swept the planted right position only, so this whole-message arm is a re-measurement on a wider slice, not a replication of v1's number.
end_to_end_power.arm_rationale: past_notch_whole and past_notch_w117 are the two completed sweeps' climbs (v2 and v3). complete_whole and complete_w117 are the same two climbs under the middle_complete ring rule, nine times the settings. oracle_past_notch is the upper bound for a split-point climb described in the rationale. W = 117 is the only window used, as v3's calibration fixed it; no other W is tested here.
end_to_end_power.sweep_decision_rule: A windowed sweep of BYQMZ is preregistered next only if windowed-117-indel-at-least-30pct, windowed-117-indel-gains-10-points and windowed-117-clean-loss-at-most-25-points all hold. It then uses W = 117 and states this run's W = 117 rates as its power. If they do not all hold, no windowed sweep is run on this evidence, whatever another window size measures; a different W would need its own calibration with a fresh seed.

conditional_analysis.status: The script is committed with this configuration and unit-tested on synthetic draws; it has not seen a result.
conditional_analysis.reference_meaning: A draw is 'missed' when neither reference arm detects it, the planted-key stand-in for both completed sweeps being null. Detection is recomputed from each draw's top candidate and each arm's own detection threshold, as the runner does.

strata.indel_middle_third: cell 1, planted position 56 to 111 inclusive, missed

predictions.statement: complete_w117 detects at least 50% of the clean missed draws.
complete_w117 detects at most 20% of the middle-third-indel missed draws.
oracle_past_notch detects at least 60% of the middle-third-indel missed draws.

yield_model.definition: Conditional detection probability given a standard Enigma I reading and both completed sweeps null, per host-hour. This is the convention of phase2-crib-prior-v1's G4 (v3: 0.29 conditional probability in about 22 host-hours, 0.013 per host-hour).
yield_model.weights: w_clean = (1 - q) * m_clean and w_indel = q * m_indel, where m is the fraction of that cell's draws that are missed and q is the prior probability, given a standard reading, that the message carries one dropped or inserted letter. q cannot be measured by any control.
yield_model.p_complete: (w_clean * a_clean + w_indel * a_indel) / (w_clean + w_indel), with a the detection rate of complete_w117 among the missed draws of that cell.
yield_model.p_split_ceiling: w_indel * o_indel / (w_clean + w_indel), with o_indel the detection rate of oracle_past_notch among the missed indel draws. A split-point climb contributes nothing on clean draws and cannot beat its oracle.
yield_model.settings_ratio_source: reducible_space_size('middle_complete') over reducible_space_size('middle_past_notch'), 246.8 million over 27.4 million, from phase1-end-to-end-power-v1
yield_model.reference_source: phase1-body-direct-sweep-v3, 16.95 h at 2.22 ms per setting on 10 workers
yield_model.break_even_cost_multiplier: k* = settings_ratio * p_split_ceiling / p_complete: the cost, in multiples of v3, at which a split-point sweep and the complete-rule sweep tie per host-hour. Below k* the split-point climb wins on cost.
yield_model.nominal_fault_prior_note: An arbitrary value declared now so that the rule below is fixed before the run. Nothing in the repository estimates q. BYQMZ carries one masked letter (position 28), which says its transcription is imperfect and nothing about a dropped letter.
yield_model.assumed_split_cost_note: An estimate, not a measurement: the shifted tail setting doubles the tables, and a joint objective over head and tail is somewhere near twice the work of a windowed climb. It is replaced by a benchmark once a split-point climb exists.

decision_rule.neither: If C1 and C3 are both refuted, neither candidate is built, and the next step is a test of the standard-reading assumption itself (see STATUS: the cited paper's footnote on Batch C's wheels).
decision_rule.complete_only: If C3 is refuted and C1 is not, the complete-rule sweep is preregistered next at its measured conditional rate.
decision_rule.split_only: If C1 is refuted and C3 is not, a split-point climb is built, calibrated against this control's draws and benchmarked, before any sweep.
decision_rule.both: If neither is refuted: the split-point climb is built and benchmarked first if k* at the nominal fault prior is at least the assumed multiplier (4); otherwise the complete-rule sweep is preregistered first. The k* values at every reported fault prior are printed so that a different belief about q can be applied without rerunning anything.
decision_rule.g4_note: The measured p_complete per host-hour replaces 0.013 as the crib-free reference in phase2-crib-prior-v1's G4. G4 is moot while G1 to G3 fail.

run_constraint: Not run. Run from a clean tree, on an idle host, with --jobs 10 (the physical core count), after the code that scores it is committed. Projected cost: 945 sweep settings per draw (45 + 45 + 405 + 405 + 45) plus null climbs; a plumbing check of three draws took 19.5 s of single-process time each, so 800 draws are about 4.3 CPU-hours, about 30 to 40 minutes on 10 workers.
limitations: The slice is the planted key's own neighbourhood: the planted wheel order, left offsets within one of the planted, middle offsets within two, and the planted right wheel. Every other wheel order and distant start is absent, so a detection is a detection against that neighbourhood and a pooled wrong-setting null, not against 2.7e7 settings. The detection threshold is set at 6 null standard deviations to stand in for the extreme value of that many draws, and that substitution assumes the null is close to normal.

The right wheel's ring and position are taken at the planted values (or, for the AAA arm, at the planted right offset with ring A). That is the one axis the full sweep enumerates exactly, so it always visits those values, but the experiment does not test it.
One plaintext prefix at one length is used for every draw. The draws vary the key, not the text, so a text that scores unusually well or badly under the published counts moves every rate together.

The null is the climb's score at randomly drawn wrong settings of the same message. It is pooled over the cell's draws, eight per draw, and is a reference distribution rather than a sample of the space a sweep would see.

The indel cell drops or inserts one random letter at a uniformly random interior position. Real garbles can be several letters, can fall in the first or last few letters, or can be a transposition; this measures the single-letter case only.
Constructed plaintext enciphered by the reference machine, not authentic held-out traffic with an authentic daily key.

The right wheel's position is swept over the planted value and its two neighbours, so the slice holds the setting one keystroke away that the tail window needs. Under the middle-past-notch rule the middle wheel's phase is fixed, so when the planted machine's first keystroke steps its middle wheel the shifted setting is not exactly reachable; the measurement includes that loss rather than assuming it away.

Each windowed arm is compared with its own pooled null, the same windowed climb at the same wrong settings, because the better of two shorter windows is distributed differently from a whole-message score. The 6-sigma threshold stands in for the extreme of a full sweep in which every setting contributes the better of two windows, which is twice as many scores as the whole-message sweep and assumes the windowed null is also near normal.

'Missed by both past-notch arms' stands in for 'v2 and v3 both null'. The real sweeps compare a candidate against a score distribution over 27.4 million settings; this control compares against a pooled null of wrong settings, as every earlier power control did. The joint figures in phase1-body-direct-sweep-v3 (73 of 80 clean) were measured the same way.

The missed set is defined by outcomes on the same draws that then measure the complete arms, so a complete arm that fails for a reason the past-notch arms share (the same unlucky plugboard) is under-counted among the missed, and one that succeeds by retrying a different equivalent setting is over-counted. Neither effect is estimated.

400 draws per cell leave about 36 clean missed draws and about 100 middle-third indel missed draws, if the rates of the earlier controls hold. A rate in a stratum of 36 has a 95% interval about 0.3 wide. The thresholds are set with that in mind and the strata sizes are reported.

The oracle is an upper bound for a split-point climb and not a measurement of one. It is handed the indel position, which a search must find, and sweeps only the past-notch slice, so keys the past-notch rule cannot reach stay missed. It says nothing about the cost of the search.

q, the prior probability of an indel, is not measured and the nominal 0.2 is arbitrary. The decision rule fixes how a given q is used and prints the break-even for several q; it does not claim any of them.

Only a single dropped or inserted letter is modelled, with the head-and-tail argument of phase1-windowed-climb-power-v1. Two faults, a substituted letter, or a fault in the first or last letters behave differently.

Detection asks for the exact planted plugboard. The oracle arm's detection threshold is the cell's whole-message null, which was measured on the unrepaired message; a repaired message differs from it by at most one letter.

Every figure assumes UKW-B, wheels I-V as wired and the 1940+ indicator procedure. The cited paper's authors suspect Batch C used differently wired wheels; if so, no planted-key power here applies to it.
